title_en: Promotion: Visiting the National Incheon Maritime Museum's Permanent and International Exchange Exhibitions
summary: This is a promotional notice; no student is required to act. Anyone interested may visit the National Incheon Maritime Museum (294 Wolmi-ro, Jemulpo-gu, Incheon) free of charge, and the international exchange exhibition "Greece, A Great Civilization Shaped by the Sea" runs until Sunday 6 December 2026. Groups of 20 or more must reserve in advance on the museum website (www.inmm.or.kr).
applies_to: Not mandatory. This is a promotional notice open to anyone interested. The notice suggests the exhibitions may be useful for field study for students of history, archaeology, art history, Western classics, maritime studies, shipbuilding, shipping, culture and tourism, and other majors. Advance reservation applies only to groups of 20 or more.

translation:
[Promotion] Information on Visiting the Permanent Exhibition and International Exchange Exhibition of the National Incheon Maritime Museum

The National Incheon Maritime Museum, the first national maritime cultural facility in the Seoul metropolitan area, is operating permanent exhibitions under the theme "Sea of Exchange, the Beginning of Connection," including the Maritime Exchange History Gallery (the history of maritime exchange), the Shipping and Ports Gallery (the development of shipping and ports) and the Maritime Culture Gallery (life and culture alongside the sea).

In addition, to commemorate the 65th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Korea and Greece, the museum is holding the international exchange exhibition "Greece, A Great Civilization Shaped by the Sea" until Sunday 6 December 2026. It is the largest Greek special exhibition ever held in Korea, presenting 348 artifacts from 15 national and public museums in Greece. It is expected to be a valuable field-study opportunity for students of various majors, including history, archaeology, art history and Western classics, as well as maritime studies, shipbuilding, shipping, culture and tourism. We encourage your interest.

A. Viewing hours (until Sunday 6 December): 10:00–18:00 (entry closes at 17:30); closed every Monday
B. Admission: Free
C. Group visits: Advance reservation via the website (www.inmm.or.kr) (groups of 20 or more)
D. Location: 294 Wolmi-ro, Jemulpo-gu, Incheon
E. Enquiries about exhibition commentary: Curator, Exhibition Planning Department (contact details are in the original notice)
